description: The keyword null can name the variadic parameter, but null in the result is still the literal
notes: The spec asks applications to treat an attribute whose value is null as if it weren't there, which would make this a function without a variadic parameter, so f(1) would have too many arguments. The native syntax spec also lets null be read as a static traversal (see native/analysis/traversal-keyword-null), which names the variadic parameter null. hashicorp/hcl reads the name with hcl.ExprAsKeyword (decodeUserFunctions in ext/userfunc/decode.go), which gives the keyword's name (LiteralValueExpr.AsTraversal in hclsyntax/expression.go), so the variadic parameter is declared, and null in the result is the literal.
